name: Seared Steak with Lemon Chive Butter, Potato-Kale Mash & Roasted Carrots (Two Ways)

ingredients.name: kale, cut and ready to use

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Cut butter into small pieces, place in a small bowl, and set aside to soften.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ lemon
½ small pkg chives

instructions.primary_message: Peel, trim, and slice carrots crosswise into ½-inch thick rounds. Transfer to a baking sheet pan. Season with salt and pepper, then spread out in an even layer. Small dice additional butter and sprinkle over the carrots.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper
butter, unsalted

instructions.primary_message: Place carrots in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until golden and fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, zest lemon into the bowl with the softened butter. (Reserve lemon for another use.)

Chop chives into small pieces; peel and mince garlic. Add half of both to the bowl, along with salt. Mash together with the back of a spoon until smooth and combined, then set the lemon-chive butter aside. (Place remaining chives and garlic in another small bowl and reserve for later use.)

Peel and medium dice potatoes. Place in a medium saucepan, add salt, then cover with hot water (from the tap). Cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat; once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook until soft, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
454 g striploin (New York strip) steak
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest.
When the potatoes are done, drain in a colander and set aside. (Reserve pan for the next step.)

Return pan to medium-high heat, add butter, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add kale (removing any thick fibrous stems) and salt; cook, stirring frequently, until kale is bright green and softened, 1-2 minutes. Transfer kale to the bowl with the reserved chives and garlic, then set aside. (Reserve pan for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
butter, unsalted
⅓ (283 g) bag kale, cut and ready to use
¼ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Return cooked potato to the pan, along with cream and spices; use a potato masher to mash until smooth. Transfer 1 cup of plain mashed potato to another plate and set aside. Add kale, chives, and garlic to the pan with the remaining potato, then stir to combine. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ cup heavy whipping cream
¼ tsp nutmeg, ground
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Thinly slice steak against the grain.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide 1 cup roasted carrots, 1 cup steak strips, and plain mashed potatoes between plates. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining carrots, steak, and potato-kale mash between plates. Top steak with lemon-chive butter and enjoy!
